correctness.rationale: All nine indices and quantifiers reconstructed: odd real determinant of 3 linear annihilator rows forces rank-one in every codimension <=3 subspace; odd cubic along any real matrix two-plane forces a nonzero singular matrix; the tracefree symmetric five-plane has precise codimension four and singular-value profile (a+b,a,b), with q>=1 triangle power bound and p<=1 subadditivity giving a sharp upper ratio attained at diag(1,-1,0); span(I_3) attains final index. All p=1, q=infinity boundaries and power-mean inequalities checked. No unproved computational conjectures.

value.rationale: Determines the exact complete nine-index Gelfand spectrum for the smallest odd real square-matrix dimension beyond 2, a natural invariant of optimal linear-measurement sections in quasi-Schatten recovery. The new early plateau c4=1 and sharp sharp drop c5 along with c6,c7 quantify the minimal measurement count needed to exclude rank one and the first exact two-singular-value width. This is not a named-parameter substitution into the known penultimate theorem and reveals real/complex field dependence at index 5. No broader paper-sized extension is presumed.
